To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
text-compression techniques can be applied to machine-readable files in order to reduce their size, and that the compression ratio is highly dependent on the type of data being compressed.

the application of text-compression methods to the nucleic acid and amino-acid sequence databases results in significant reductions of the storage requirements of the databases, and that the compression figures are higher for the nucleic-acid sequence database than for the amino-acid sequence database.
text compression can be applied effectively to machine-readable files containing nucleic acid or protein sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the compression of nucleic acid sequence data.
the development and implementation of text compression methods that can be applied to machine-readable nucleic acid and/or protein sequence data.
the application of text-compression methods to nucleic acid and peptide sequence data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of text compression methods can significantly reduce the storage requirements associated with machine-readable files of sequence data.
the compression figures achieved by these techniques were very impressive.
text compression methods can be applied to machine-readable files to produce substantial compression of nucleic acid sequence data, and that this is not the case for protein sequence data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can store the GenBank and Protein Identification Resource databases with an estimated 75% and 43% compression, respectively.
the use of text compression techniques can be used to reduce the size of nucleic acid/protein sequence files by up to 75%.
we have developed a method that is simple to use, is fast, and can achieve a compression figure of about 50% for a wide range of biological data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
text compression methods can be successfully applied to the compression of biological sequence data, with a significant improvement in compression figures over existing techniques.
text compression methods can be used to reduce the size of nucleic acid/protein data bases and that this is an area worthy of further investigation.
the storage requirements of nucleic acid sequence data can be greatly reduced by the use of text compression methods.
